summary: Make the historical database migrations replay safely on Oracle and PostgreSQL, so partially populated Oracle schemas no longer fail with ORA-00902 or ORA-01758, and nullability or type changes keep existing data.
userImpact: Oracle databases that replay the historical migration epoch no longer stop with ORA-00902 (invalid datatype) or ORA-01758 (table must be empty to add mandatory column).
Migrations that relax or tighten NOT NULL on populated Oracle tables change the column in place instead of dropping and re-adding it, so role-assignment and deployment-lineage data is preserved.
Oracle installations whose Camunda native-grant import evidence was stored as VARCHAR2 are widened to CLOB without losing the stored classifications or encrypted snapshots.

notes: Existing migrations were corrected in place; no new migration is added and already-applied migrations are not re-run.
Legacy migrations resolve column types for the connected database. PostgreSQL schemas built from text columns receive the same DDL as before.
Nullability changes clone the live column, so Oracle receives MODIFY ... [NOT] NULL and PostgreSQL receives ALTER COLUMN ... SET/DROP NOT NULL with data intact.
On Oracle, migration 100 widens VARCHAR2 evidence to CLOB through a staging column (add, copy, drop, rename). Each step checks the live schema, so a rerun resumes an interrupted widening.
A bootstrap that runs synchronize() before replaying the epoch still stops at AddReleaseEffectCohorts1700000000131 by design; that schema-epoch guard is unchanged.

knownLimitations: A schema-epoch bootstrap that has already created release_effect_cohorts through synchronize() is still refused by migration 131 on every database.
rollback: Redeploy the previous shared package or application image. Widened Oracle CLOB evidence columns and relaxed or tightened nullability are retained; automatic schema shrinking is unsupported.
validation: Live Oracle XE 21c: fresh schema, idempotent rerun and a full replay of all 136 migrations over a seeded schema with relaxed NOT NULL columns passed.
Live PostgreSQL 18: fresh schema, idempotent rerun and a full replay of all 135 applicable migrations passed.

Live Oracle migration 100: VARCHAR2(4000) evidence including a 3990-character value was widened to CLOB with every value and the original nullability preserved, and a widening interrupted after the drop step resumed correctly.
Live Oracle and PostgreSQL: relaxing NOT NULL on a populated column kept its value with the new helper, while the previous pattern emptied it.
Backend unit tests passed, including all migration tests in backend/__tests__/shared/db.
